tier_reason: First-party chart only (docs/source/media/benchmark_results_001.svg) produced by the public tests/benchmark.py, with CPU (Ryzen 5 3400G) and NumPy 2.3.5 stated but no Python version, GCC version, or statement of whether the stencils came from the PyPI wheel or tools/build.sh; the raw results JSON is not committed (404). Partial methodology on the project's own harness is tier C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README chart only, no numbers in text. Read from the SVG marker coordinates (derived from page data): 30,000 iterations take about 0.079 s for Copapy versus 0.308 s for NumPy 2.3.5 at v_size 10 (about 3.9x, roughly 2.6 versus 10.3 microseconds per iteration), 0.125 s versus 0.351 s at v_size 100 (about 2.8x), and 0.321 s versus 0.555 s at v_size 500 (about 1.7x). The absolute gap stays near 7.7 microseconds per iteration at every size, so the lead is NumPy's per-call overhead; the slopes are nearly equal.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: x86_64 stencils are built by tools/build.sh with gcc -fno-pic -ffunction-sections -O3 (Target default optimization 'O3'); the GCC version, the Python version and whether the benchmark used the PyPI wheel or a local build are not stated.
corrections.caveats: Baseline is NumPy 2.3.5 (float32 arrays), not PyPy, V8, LuaJIT or HotSpot; the win is small-vector call overhead: the gap is a constant ~7.7 microseconds per iteration from v_size 10 to 500 (derived from the chart), so the ratio shrinks from about 3.9x to 1.7x as vectors grow. Numbers exist only as a chart image; the results JSON the script writes is not in the repo. The Copapy case calls tg.run() (which still builds a small command buffer in Python and calls the in-process coparun runner) and never reads the result back, while the NumPy case returns a scalar each iteration; the README discloses that no data moves between Python and compiled code. The work is real, not a no-op: cp.value inputs are non-anonymous constants that the compiler keeps as runtime data. Harness nits: the pure-Python row runs iter_size//100 iterations but records iter_size//10 (that row is not plotted), and the unused cp_vs_python_sparse function contains an 'assert False'. A @cp.jit decorator exists for ordinary Python functions, but the README benchmark does not cover it and says cp.jit is not optimized for data transfer.

tier_reason: The only numbers are WebSearch snippets of arXiv 1507.02437 (paper not opened: ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org EGRESS_BLOCKED, arxiv.org blocked by policy); the README has no benchmarks. The repo does carry the 26-benchmark list (source/benchmark-list.csv: 19 SunSpider plus 7 V8 benchmark suite programs) and runner (source/benchmark.py with --vm_cmd), but hardware, V8 version and flags cannot be checked, so snippet-only evidence stays at C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Snippet only (paper not opened): with typed shapes and shape propagation, Higgs outperforms the V8 baseline (non-optimizing) compiler on all but one of 26 benchmarks, with speedups of up to 682%; it lags behind V8's Crankshaft (run without inlining, per one snippet), which performs 49% better on average. Abstract (snippet): the techniques eliminate on average 48% of type tests, reduce code size by 17% and reduce execution time by 25% versus Higgs with plain polymorphic inline caches.
corrections.caveats: Weak claim: it beats only V8's old full-codegen baseline compiler (removed from V8 in 2017) and loses to Crankshaft by 49% on average; no comparison exists against any current engine. Numbers are from WebSearch snippets of arXiv 1507.02437, which could not be opened here, so hardware, V8 version and flags are unverified. Venue unverified: search results describe the paper as a CoRR/arXiv technical report from Universite de Montreal; the record's 'DLS 2015' label could not be confirmed, so it is not treated as peer-reviewed. The benchmark list and a Python 2 runner (source/benchmark.py) are in the repo. Licence: no LICENSE file and no GitHub licence badge; source headers (e.g. source/main.d) carry a three-clause Modified BSD licence; JS runtime and library files were not checked. Last commit 2023-06-09 (Python 3 build fix, PR #218); the previous commit was 2019.
